secrets.name: website/payload-secret
secrets.consequence: Restart the CMS; every editorial session ends (Payload signs its session tokens with it).

secrets.name: website/lifecycle-intake
secrets.consumer: cms.env and web.env LIFECYCLE_INTAKE_SECRET (one shared value)
secrets.consequence: CMS and website restart together; an apply or redeem in flight at that moment fails once.

secrets.name: identity/client/terrace-web
secrets.consequence: Keycloak keeps its own copy: rotate --manual, push (consumers restart on the new value), then on the host `terrace-identity-admin client-secret sync --client terrace-web` sets Keycloak to it and checks the old value is refused; sign-ins through this client fail between push and sync.

secrets.name: identity/client/terrace-community
secrets.consequence: Keycloak keeps its own copy: rotate --manual, push (consumers restart on the new value), then on the host `terrace-identity-admin client-secret sync --client terrace-community` sets Keycloak to it and checks the old value is refused; sign-ins through this client fail between push and sync.

secrets.name: identity/database-password
secrets.consumer: Keycloak PostgreSQL role (created once by keycloakPostgreSQLInit)
secrets.consequence: rotate --manual, then `apply` (ALTER ROLE over the pinned channel), then push; Keycloak restarts.

secrets.name: identity/bootstrap-admin-password
secrets.consumer: escrow only: delivered once by `apply` to /run/terrace-identity-admin for `terrace-identity-admin first-admin`
secrets.consequence: Single use for the first administrator: `apply` it to the host, run first-admin, then rotate --manual. Never declared on a production host.

secrets.name: tls/certificate
secrets.consumer: nginx certificate chain for every public hostname of the role
secrets.consequence: Replace with `set` and push; nginx restarts.

secrets.name: tls/key
secrets.consequence: Replace with `set` together with the certificate and push; nginx restarts.

secrets.name: backup/primary/repository-password
secrets.consequence: rotate --manual, `apply` (restic key add), push, `apply --finish` (restic key remove of the old key); escrow is the store.

secrets.name: backup/primary/sftp-key
secrets.consumer: restic primary SFTP identity (public half enrolled at the Storage Box)
secrets.consequence: rotate --manual, enrol the new public half at the Storage Box, push, then remove the old public key there.

secrets.name: backup/secondary/repository-password
secrets.consequence: As the primary repository password, on the secondary target.

secrets.name: backup/secondary/environment
secrets.consumer: restic secondary environmentFile (B2 S3 key id and key)
secrets.consequence: Create a new application key at the provider, `set`, push, then delete the old key at the provider.
